household: with his grandfather's household (Book I, 'Washington Square')
creator: Hanya Yanagihara
notes: All three books of the novel are set in the same townhouse on Washington Square, in an alternate-history New York in Book I. No house number is given; the point sits on Washington Square North, the row Henry James's Washington Square evokes.
source_quote: To combine the three stories she had developed into a single novel, Yanagihara set each in the same townhouse adjacent Washington Square Park.

creator: Hanya Yanagihara
address_as_given: the same townhouse adjacent Washington Square Park
notes: In the 1993 section, 25-year-old David lives with his older lover Charles, a wealthy lawyer, in the Washington Square townhouse. Wikipedia says only that each book is set in the same townhouse; no number is given.
source_quote: In 1993 David Bingham is a 25-year-old paralegal descended from Hawaiian royalty who has chosen to turn his back on his heritage and lives in New York City with Charles Griffiths, a wealthy older lawyer.
source2_quote: To combine the three stories she had developed into a single novel, Yanagihara set each in the same townhouse adjacent Washington Square Park.

creator: Jennifer Egan
address_as_given: the Styles mansion on the shore of Manhattan Beach in Brooklyn
notes: The gangster Dexter Styles's waterfront house, where 11-year-old Anna Kerrigan first meets him in late 1934. No street is given. The Kerrigans' own apartment is not placed by any source found.
source_quote: Eleven-going-on-twelve Anna Kerrigan and her father, Eddie, meet with gangster Dexter Styles, in late 1934, at the Styles mansion on the shore of Manhattan Beach in Brooklyn, New York City.

creator: Riley Sager (Todd Ritter)
address_as_given: the Bartholomew, a sliver of stone rising thirteen stories over Central Park West
notes: The Bartholomew is an invented building, a Dakota-like Gothic apartment house with gargoyles; From 12A Jules looks out on the Lake and Bow Bridge, which puts it around West 74th Street. The point is an estimate. Jules sits the apartment for a few weeks before she flees.
source_quote: the Bartholomew is a mere wisp of a thing-a sliver of stone rising thirteen stories over Central Park West.
source2_quote: With no job prospects, Jules answers a job posting for an apartment sitter in an exclusive building called The Bartholomew.

creator: Ursula Parrott
address_as_given: an apartment toward the western border of Greenwich village
notes: The narrator and Pete move here early in the marriage, after money troubles; it had a roof where they sat on August nights. No street is named. Setting years are estimates; the novel spans the mid-to-late 1920s.
source_quote: We moved to an apartment toward the western border of Greenwich village. It had a roof, where we sat, hot August nights

creator: Ursula Parrott
neighborhood: Park Avenue (Midtown East / Upper East Side)
notes: After the divorce Patricia shares a top-floor apartment with Lucia, rent $175 a month. The novel names only Park Avenue; the point is a guess at the residential stretch in the East 60s, so the radius is wide.
source_quote: We had what we called a garret, on Park Avenue. The rent was a hundred and seventy-five dollars a month

creator: Tim Murphy
notes: The real Christodora House, a 16-story 1928 building at Avenue B and East 9th Street facing Tompkins Square Park. The novel runs from the early 1980s to the 2020s; the couple's years in the building are approximate. The Village Voice notes they pay $90,000 for a two-bedroom.
source_quote: On Avenue B in the heart of the Lower East Side, the Christodora is home to Milly and Jared, a privileged young couple with artistic ambitions.
source2_quote: the sixteen-story Christodora House, which sits on Avenue B across from Tompkins Square Park, was not just an edifice, but a metaphor.

creator: Tim Murphy
address_as_given: the Christodora, on Avenue B (Milly and Jared's neighbor)
notes: The former AIDS activist who lives in the building as Milly and Jared's neighbor. Years are approximate.
source_quote: the Christodora is home to Milly and Jared, a privileged young couple with artistic ambitions. Their neighbor, Hector, a Puerto Rican gay man

household: near the tinsmith Boutros Arbeely's shop
creator: Helene Wecker
address_as_given: Washington Street, west of here, near a tinsmith's shop
notes: The jinni tells Chava where he lives. Little Syria ran along Washington Street south of the World Trade Center site; most of it was razed for the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel approaches. No number is given.
source_quote: I live on Washington Street, west of here, near a tinsmith's shop.
source2_quote: Meanwhile, a tinsmith in New York's Little Syria accidentally frees a jinni from a flask in which he has been imprisoned for a millennium.

household: with her parents, grandparents and siblings
creator: Jacqueline Dembar Greene
address_as_given: the Lower East Side of New York City
notes: Six-book American Girl series set in 1914. Wikipedia names only the Lower East Side; no street was found in a source.
source_quote: She is a 9-year-old Russian Jewish girl whose maternal grandparents and parents immigrated to the Lower East Side of New York City in 1914.

creator: Donald E. Westlake
address_as_given: an apartment in Manhattan on East 19th Street
notes: Dortmunder's recurring home across the series, shared with May from Bank Shot (1972) on. Only the street is given; the point is mid-block near Third Avenue and could sit anywhere along East 19th.
source_quote: He shares an apartment in Manhattan on East 19th Street with longtime girlfriend May Bellamy, a supermarket cashier.

household: with his mother, a cab driver
creator: Donald E. Westlake
notes: The gang's driver, a recurring character from The Hot Rock on. Only the neighborhood is given.
source_quote: Murch lives in Canarsie with his cab-driver mother

household: with her parents, Joseph and Leah, and sister Tina
creator: Min Jin Lee
address_as_given: their small apartment in Elmhurst, Queens
notes: Casey's parents' apartment, where she returns after Princeton until her father throws her out early in the novel. Joseph and Leah stay on in Elmhurst. No street is given.
source_quote: Casey Han has just graduated from Princeton University and returned to live with her Korean immigrant parents, Joseph and Leah, and her younger sister Tina, in their small apartment in Elmhurst, Queens.

household: with her husband Jack, the library's superintendent, and their two children
creator: Fiona Davis
address_as_given: the superintendent's apartment inside the New York Public Library
notes: The 1913 storyline is set in the real seven-room superintendent's apartment inside the library's main building at Fifth Avenue and 42nd Street. The Lyons family is invented; the apartment was real.
source_quote: Davis discovered that there had been a seven-room apartment inside that housed its superintendent and his family.
source2_quote: which interweaves the story of the fictional wife of the superintendent in 1913 with her granddaughter's, who serves as a curator at the library in 1993.

household: with her anarchist father, a printer
creator: Hernan Diaz
address_as_given: at home with her father in Brooklyn (Carroll Gardens, per the author's tour)
notes: Ida lives with her father in Brooklyn's Italian enclave while she ghostwrites for Andrew Bevel. Diaz showed a Vanity Fair writer the Carroll Gardens street where some characters live but the article does not name it.
source_quote: On a tour of Carroll Gardens, he points out the street where some of his characters live, historic landmarks, and iconic Italian American bakeries.
source2_quote: She lives at home with her radical anarchist father (a character heavily inspired by Diaz's own father) in Brooklyn

creator: Gary Shteyngart
address_as_given: the Alphabet City neighborhood of Manhattan
notes: Wikipedia places the New York half of the novel in Alphabet City and says Vladimir shares an apartment with Challah, but does not tie the two together in one sentence. He later lives with Francesca's family before fleeing to Prava.
source_quote: It follows the exploits of young Russians, both in the Alphabet City neighborhood of Manhattan and in the European city of Prava (a pseudonym for Prague).
source2_quote: He shares an apartment with his girlfriend, an overweight redhead named Challah who works as a dominatrix.

creator: Cristina Alger
notes: The novel unfolds over Thanksgiving week 2008. Only Park Avenue is named; the point is a guess on the Upper East Side stretch, which reviews say is the book's world.
source_quote: attorney Paul Ross has grown accustomed to New York society and all of its luxuries: a Park Avenue apartment, weekends in the Hamptons, bespoke suits.
source2_quote: The Darlings live the good life on Park Avenue and in the Hamptons
